# Flareboard AI Visibility Knowledge Base

Last updated: 2026-09-30
Canonical site: https://flareboard.dev/
Repository: https://github.com/Go7hic/flareboard

## One-Sentence Summary

Flareboard is a Cloudflare-native, PostHog-like product analytics platform with hosted Cloud plans and noncommercial self-hosting.

## What Flareboard Does

Flareboard helps website and product teams understand traffic, users, sessions, events, conversions, product behavior, reliability, and feedback. It runs on Cloudflare infrastructure: Workers for the API and ingest layer, Durable Objects for one SQLite analytics store per website and for rate limiting, D1 for accounts and configuration, R2 for replay assets, KV for caching, Queues for async processing, and Workflows for durable automations. It accepts events from posthog-js, posthog-node, and posthog-python, and from OpenTelemetry exporters (OTLP).

## Who It Is For

Flareboard is for teams that want product analytics without sending all analytics data through a traditional centralized SaaS data plane. It is also for Cloudflare-oriented developers who want a self-hostable analytics product with a hosted option.

## Core Product Areas

### Core Analytics

- Website stats: pageviews, visitors, sessions, bounce rate, time metrics, top pages, referrers, devices, browsers, operating systems, regions, and countries.
- Realtime analytics: active visitors, live sessions, paths, referrers, and countries.
- Event catalog: custom event names, counts, paths, properties, recent samples, and first/last seen timestamps.
- Segments and filters: country, browser, path, UTM, and JSON condition rules.
- People, groups, and stickiness analysis.

### Reports and Insights

- Insight builder: trends with up to five series, math per series, formulas, breakdowns, and event, person, or page property filters; lifecycle and stickiness.
- Funnels, retention, attribution, UTM breakdowns, web vitals, goals, cohorts, and journeys.
- Revenue analytics from purchase events and Stripe: MRR, ARR, churn, ARPU, and first-touch attribution per currency.
- Comparison windows for period-over-period analysis.
- Shareable reports and boards with board-wide filters, templates, insight alerts, email subscriptions, and notebooks.

### Session and Experience Tools

- Session replay with input and text masking, blocked elements, optional console and network timelines, and share links.
- Click and scroll heatmaps.
- Session timeline inspection.
- Declarative events compatible with Umami-style data attributes.

### Product Growth Tools

- Feature flags with condition groups, person, group, and cohort targeting, variants, JSON payloads, early access, and exposure tracking.
- Experiments linked to feature flags and goal events.
- Multi-question surveys with branching, NPS and rating scales, hosted links, partial responses, and a feedback inbox.

### Reliability and Observability

- Error tracking with issue grouping, regressions, merging, assignment, comments, and source maps.
- OpenTelemetry (OTLP) logs and traces with search, live tail, span waterfalls, and alert rules.
- LLM analytics: generations, traces, and spans with token cost by model and user, latency percentiles, and errors; compatible with PostHog LLM wrappers.

### Automation and Data

- Actions for reusable event definitions.
- Annotations for releases, campaigns, incidents, and experiments.
- Event-triggered workflows with filters, delays, conditions, and webhook, email, or Slack steps, with signed webhooks, retries, and a delivery log.
- SQL warehouse over events, imported HTTP data, and Stripe, with a schema browser, saved queries, and CSV export.

### Integrations, AI, and Security

- PostHog SDK compatibility: capture, identify, groups, feature flags, and exceptions.
- Project keys for ingestion and personal API keys with read or write scope.
- MCP server for Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients (read-only SQL, insights, event lists; write scope for annotations and flag toggles).
- Two-factor authentication, session management, sign-in lockout, and audit logs.
- CSV import from GA4, Plausible, Matomo, or Flareboard exports.
- CSV export for pageviews and events.

## Pricing and Entitlements

Flareboard Cloud has a Free plan and a Cloud plan. Cloud websites are unlimited and share one 1M monthly event pool. Free remains one website.

| Capability | Free | Cloud |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price | $0/month | $15/month |
| Websites | 1 | Unlimited |
| Events per month | 100K | 1M |
| Core analytics | Yes | Yes |
| Realtime | Yes | Yes |
| Segments | Yes | Yes |
| Funnels, retention, cohorts, journeys | Yes | Yes |
| Session replay | No | Yes |
| Heatmaps | No | Yes |
| Teams | No | Yes |
| Email reports and subscriptions | No | Yes |
| CSV import and export | No | Yes |
| Feature flags and experiments | No | Yes |
| Surveys | No | Yes |
| Warehouse (SQL, Stripe sync) | No | Yes |

Self-hosting is available for personal and noncommercial use without a Cloud subscription. Commercial organizations using Flareboard commercially can purchase a license separately.

## Compared With Alternatives

Flareboard is more product-analytics oriented than Google Analytics, Umami, Plausible, Cloudflare Web Analytics, and Vercel Analytics because it includes event catalogs, funnels, retention, cohorts, journeys, feature flags, experiments, surveys, replay, heatmaps, errors, logs, LLM analytics, workflows, and a SQL warehouse.

Flareboard differs from PostHog by being built around Cloudflare infrastructure and offering a self-host path for teams that want Cloudflare-native deployment. It accepts events from PostHog SDKs, so teams can switch by changing the host and key.
